subject: Footprint pricing and module swap — pilot offer for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@skylinehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring a smaller footprint for our pilot: modules and credits

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like the latency profile, but we're constrained on budget for this pilot and need to keep the GPU footprint small while proving value. A couple quick questions:

- Can we run a reduced-feature pilot (no embeddings, just chat + reranking) and still keep a single SLA?
- How do you price feature gating — is it per-seat, per-token, or a modular addon?
- Would you consider an introductory credit + 20% pilot discount if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract after pilot success?

I can loop in procurement if helpful.

—Miguel
Miguel Alvarez
Head of Infrastructure
Skyline Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a smaller footprint for our pilot: modules and credits

Miguel — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, then a proposal: 

- Yes: a reduced-feature pilot (chat + reranking only) is common and can be covered under our standard SLA for pilots; we treat embeddings and heavy-batch jobs separately.
- Pricing for gated features: we typically treat them as modular line-items on top of the base per-token generation price (eg: +X% for embeddings or per-1000-embedding units). For pilots we can translate those to temporary credits rather than permanent surcharges.
- We can offer an introductory credit plus a pilot discount, but discount depth depends on expected committed capacity (tokens/day) and whether you want Dedicated capacity.

Proposal (what I'll price and send formally):
1) Pilot scope: chat + reranking only, 2 vCPU + 1 GPU equivalent footprint, 10k request cap/day.
2) Pilot commercial: $12,000 credit applied over 30 days + 18% pilot discount on hosted per-token while pilot active.
3) Conversion offer: if you sign a 12-month Dedicated contract within 30 days of pilot completion, credit becomes $6k in onboarding credit and we add a 10% ramp discount for 3 months.

Ben — can you run the numbers in the attached pricing model and confirm impact to list and margin? Priyom — want your take on feature gating (how to implement safe fallbacks and keep reranking cost low). Lauren — flag any standard legal/SoW items we should include for a quick DocuSign.

I'll follow up with a draft SoW and the pricing CSV.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a smaller footprint for our pilot: modules and credits

Jordan / team — ran a quick model (attached: pilot-pricing-model-v2.csv). Key points: 

- The 2 vCPU + 1 GPU footprint with chat + rerank only reduces expected token volume by ~45% vs full suite. Gross margin at 18% pilot discount remains healthy for hosted trial but is thin if we also provide large onboarding credits.
- If Skyline converts to Dedicated at a modest commit (approx. $25k/mo committed spend), we can offer the conversion uplift you suggested: onboarding credit conversion + 10% ramp. That keeps unit economics intact.
- Alternative: keep hosted for pilot and offer a 25% conversion credit (one-time) instead of a lower onboarding credit — more attractive to procurement and easier legally.

Attachments: pilot-pricing-model-v2.csv (breakdown by SKU), suggested language for conversion credit in SoW.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring a smaller footprint for our pilot: modules and credits

Quick note on gating and fallback:

- For cost control, implement per-route limits and a soft-cache for common prompts. Reranking can be configured to only call models when confidence < threshold — that reduces per-request token volume.
- Feature toggle approach: expose "reranker_enabled" flag in the API key metadata; during pilot we can keep it on for 10% of traffic and ramp to 100% on success.
- In the SoW, include an acceptance criteria bullet: "<business metric> improves by X% over baseline within pilot window" so procurement has a clear conversion gate.

I'll add a one-paragraph implementation note to the SoW.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
